question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation after a stimulus pulse
ideas.description: Use a degron-tagged FOS or JUN allele (e.g., dTAG or auxin-inducible) to degrade AP-1 at defined times after a single stimulus. If AP-1 is the memory mechanism, the later response to restimulation should be lost or reduced when AP-1 is removed during the rest period, but not when it is removed before the first stimulus.

ideas.title: Time-course of chromatin persistence after AP-1 occupancy is lost
ideas.description: After a stimulus pulse, run ATAC-seq, H3K27ac/H3K4me1 CUT&RUN, and FOS/JUN CUT&RUN at several time points during washout. A memory mechanism predicts that enhancers keep open or primed chromatin after AP-1 leaves them, and that this persistence depends on the AP-1 motifs and on the stimulus having occurred.

ideas.title: Motif-mutation test of recall at endogenous memory loci
ideas.description: Use CRISPR base editing or prime editing to mutate AP-1 motifs at enhancers of genes that show a primed, faster response on restimulation. Compare the stimulus-recall response (fold induction and kinetics) of mutant and wild-type cells in a rested-then-restimulated paradigm to test whether the motifs are required for memory.

ideas.title: Single-cell tracking of AP-1 history through divisions
ideas.description: Combine a live AP-1 activity reporter (for example, a destabilized fluorescent protein under an AP-1-responsive or Fos promoter) with lineage barcodes and single-cell multiome readout. Compare cells with different prior AP-1 histories to see whether the prior state is inherited by daughter cells and predicts their later response, which separates a heritable memory from stochastic cell-to-cell variation.

ideas.title: Engram-style necessity test in vivo
ideas.description: In a mouse model such as hippocampal engram or tissue-resident immune memory, label cells active during a learning or priming event with an activity-dependent tag (for example, a Fos-based TRAP system). Then use time-restricted dominant-negative or conditional Fos/Jun inhibition during consolidation or recall, and measure whether the memory-dependent reactivation and the tagged cells' chromatin state are disrupted.
